events.objective: Establish the true symptom timeline and blast radius for INC-008: when did auth-service p99 latency and 503 rate first deviate from baseline (the reporter says the release pattern reminds them of last year, but we need the actual onset)? Is the degradation isolated to auth-service, or are other services (gateway, user-service, session/token stores, DB-facing services) showing elevated latency/errors in the same window? Characterize the error signatures on /v1/auth/login (timeouts vs 5xx from upstream vs 503 from the app) and check resource trends (CPU, memory, connection pool saturation, thread pool) on auth-service and any shared downstream dependency over 2026-04-22 05:00-09:00.

Find what changed ahead of the incident across ALL services, not just auth-service: list deployments, config changes, feature flags, and infrastructure changes in the 2026-04-21 to 2026-04-22 08:59 window, with exact timestamps and versions. Map auth-service's dependencies and dependents (what it calls, what calls it, shared components like DBs, caches, load balancers, secrets/identity providers) so we can tell whether a change in a neighboring or shared component could explain login failures. Also retrieve the historical incident record for last year's bcrypt regression (root cause, trigger, blast radius) to compare against.

Correlate the change set from task b against the onset time established in task a and against auth-service's dependency graph: identify which single change (or combination) temporally precedes the first deviation and plausibly touches the login path -- e.g. an auth-service release with a bcrypt cost/rounds change, a change in an upstream identity/secret dependency, a config change on a shared component, or a resource/capacity change. Compare the current signatures with the last-year bcrypt incident to confirm or rule out that hypothesis, and state the most likely fault location (which service actually owns the defect).

events.statement: Only one deployment exists across all services in the incident window: portfolio-service v4.4.0 deployed 2026-04-22T05:50:00Z (author ci-bot, 'Holdings export', changes ['CSV export endpoint'], status live, rolled_back_at null). No auth-service release and no rollback appear.

The same near-empty change set holds with the window widened back to 2026-04-18, so the 04-21→04-22 result is not an artifact of a too-narrow window: still exactly 1 deployment (dep-5803) and 1 config change (cfg-2801) in the 4-day span.
The single config change is auth-service log.level INFO→WARN at 2026-04-22T03:40:00Z by config-bot, description 'Reduce log volume' — a logging-verbosity change, ~3h22m before the 07:06Z report.

Dependency map for auth-service: outbound edges to user-db (kind db), redis-cache (kind cache), kyc-provider (kind external); inbound edge api-gateway → auth-service (kind http). Node types: api-gateway/edge, user-db/postgres, redis-cache/redis (shared:true), kyc-provider/external with has_telemetry:false.
redis-cache is the only shared datastore in auth-service's map (shared:true), while user-db is a non-shared postgres; querying redis-cache downstream returned an empty edge list (no callees)

Historical precedent HIST-101 (2025-08-14, 'Login latency after auth-service release') with symptoms 'login p99 4s', '503 on login', 'high cpu'; root cause 'bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0', category bad_deployment, resolution 'Rolled back v6.4.0'. Its blast radius was auth-service only. Related past incidents: HIST-108 (2025-10-01, JWT signing-key rotation, 401s), HIST-107 (2025-12-09, redis cold-cache storm), HIST-109 (2025-07-11 token validation).

The HIST-101 analog does not match the change record: HIST-101's trigger was a code release (v6.4.0) but no auth-service or any-service release/rollback occurred in this window, so the observed change feed gives no deployment-side explanation for a bcrypt-style regression.

events.description: No feature-flag change-log tool was available in my toolset; my calls covered deployments and config changes only, so flags could not be enumerated for the window.
kyc-provider is an external node with has_telemetry:false and no deployment/change record; its status/change history is not observable from this toolset.

redis-cache returned no downstream edges ("edges":[]) and I ran out of budget before querying its available_metrics for a failover/eviction/connection signal around 07:00Z; HIST-107 shows redis failover can cause shared-component storms.
No infrastructure-change feed was queried (budget exhausted); the deployment/config tools returned only application-level changes.

events.answer: Across ALL services in the 2026-04-21 → 2026-04-22 08:59 window there is only one deployment (portfolio-service v4.4.0, "Holdings export", 05:50Z, live/not rolled back) and one config change (auth-service log.level INFO→WARN, 03:40Z, log-volume only). No auth-service deployment, no feature-flag change, and no rollback appears anywhere near the onset — so, unlike HIST-101, this does not look like a fresh auth-service release. auth-service depends on user-db (postgres, non-shared), redis-cache (SHARED redis), the external kyc-provider (no telemetry), and is called by api-gateway; redis-cache is the only shared component that could carry a neighbouring failure into login.

events.statement: auth-service p99 latency was flat at ~88–91ms from 05:00 through 06:40, then jumped to avg 2288.53ms (max 4012.81) in the 06:50 bucket and stayed ~3770–3867ms through 08:50. Onset is the 06:50–07:00 bucket.
auth-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) was ~0.2% until 06:40, then rose to avg 7.11% (max 14.76) in the 06:50 bucket and ~14% thereafter (e.g. 14.13% at 08:50). Same onset bucket as latency.

auth-service error signature on /v1/auth/login is app-generated 503s from accept-queue overflow plus worker-pool saturation, not downstream timeouts: top pattern 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning <n> (POST /v<n>/auth/login)' count=372 first_seen 06:55:42; 'worker pool saturated (active=64/64, queue=<n>)' count=249 first_seen 06:54:53 (e.g. queue=39035, queue=98763), and 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' at 06:57:15.
auth-service CPU jumped from a stable ~37–38% baseline (05:00–06:40) to avg 84.31% (max 97.33) in the 06:50 bucket and ~97% thereafter, coincident with the latency/error onset.

auth-service memory stayed flat (~47–57%, avg ~52%) across the entire 05:00–09:00 window including after onset (e.g. 51.46% at 06:50, 51.76% last), so memory is NOT a contributing trend; CPU is the deviating resource.

api-gateway p99 latency is NOT isolated: it was flat ~206–213ms through 06:40, then jumped to avg 2441.06ms (max 4200.87) in the same 06:50 bucket and ~3920ms thereafter — matching the auth-service onset bucket, consistent with gateway inheriting auth-service latency.

Log query for auth-service was truncated (returned 30 of 657 matched, truncated:true), so absence of other error patterns (e.g. timeouts) is not proven.

events.answer: auth-service p99 latency first deviated at the 06:50–07:00 bucket (avg 2288ms at 06:50, then 3770ms at 07:00) and error rate jumped in the same bucket (0.21% → 7.11% at 06:50 → 14.12% at 07:00), with the first logged 503 ("accept queue full") at 06:55:42 and worker-pool saturation WARNs starting 06:54:53 — i.e. onset ~06:54–06:55, before the 07:06 report. The degradation is NOT isolated: api-gateway p99 rose in the exact same bucket (211ms → 2441ms at 06:50 → 3921ms at 07:00), consistent with gateway latency being a downstream reflection of auth-service. The error signature on /v1/auth/login is app-level 503s from accept-queue/worker-pool saturation (active=64/64, queue up to 98763), not downstream timeouts; auth-service CPU jumped from ~38% to ~97% at 06:50 while memory stayed flat at ~52%.

events.statement: Widening the query window does not change the near-empty change set: even over a month (2026-03-22 → 2026-04-22) for redis-cache the config-change count is 0, and for portfolio-service over 05:00-08:59 on 04-22 the count is 0 — so no shared-component or neighbour config change coincides with the onset.

auth-service's full dependency map (downstream direction) confirms exactly three outbound edges — user-db (postgres, non-shared), redis-cache (redis, shared:true) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry:false) — so the only neighbours that could inject a fault into the login path are the shared redis-cache and the untraced kyc-provider.

redis-cache is shared by five callers (auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service) plus api-gateway/http edges, so a redis degradation could in principle transit to login — but there is no redis config change and no adjacency to a deployed change, and the multi-service redis caller set shows no onboarding change in the window.

The nearest precedent in the wider incident search is HIST-113 (2026-01-28, pricing-engine CPU saturation at market open, root cause 'Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity', category capacity_saturation) — pre-scaled/raised replicas as resolution — which matches the current CPU-saturation-with-autoscaler-cap signature more closely than HIST-101 (bcrypt bad deployment).

HIST-101 (2025-08-14) is the only login+503+high-CPU precedent and its category is bad_deployment with resolution 'Rolled back v6.4.0'; no rollout or rollback of any version exists in the current window, so the current incident cannot be a replay of the same trigger by the change feed alone (it could still share the symptom profile without a release).

The auth-service log.level INFO→WARN change at 2026-04-22T03:40:00Z is the sole auth-service-touching change; it is verbosity-only ('Reduce log volume') and precedes onset by ~3h10m, with no plausible mechanism to raise CPU from 38% to 97% (it would if anything reduce I/O), so it is not a temporal/causal match for the 06:50 onset.

events.description: Could not retrieve metric series for redis-cache, user-db or kyc-provider to test whether a shared-dependency degradation preceded the 06:50 auth-service onset: the get_config_changes/get_deployments calls returned empty for those components and I exhausted budget before issuing component metric queries (available_metrics then values).
No autoscaler/HPA configuration history (maxReplicas=8) was retrieved; only the runtime log line 'desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8' is available from T1.
kyc-provider is external with has_telemetry:false and no change feed, so its health/version around onset is unobservable.
No k8s node/container resource-request or limits change record exists in the change feed for auth-service.

events.answer: No change in the 2026-04-21→04-22 08:59 window temporally precedes the 06:50-06:55 onset or touches the login path: the only deployment is portfolio-service v4.4.0 (05:50Z, unrelated) and the only config change is auth-service log.level INFO→WARN (03:40Z, log-only). The bcrypt-release hypothesis is not supported by the change record (no code release anywhere), and no shared-component (redis-cache) config change exists; the observed signature (CPU 38%→97%, accept-queue/worker-pool saturation, autoscaler capped at maxReplicas 8, memory flat) points to per-instance CPU/thread-pool capacity saturation inside auth-service itself rather than an upstream/shared-dependency fault. auth-service owns the defect; whether the trigger is external request-load rather than a change cannot be decided from the change feed alone.

events.title: Capacity saturation: login traffic outran provisioned auth-service capacity (HPA capped at maxReplicas=8)
Recurrence of HIST-101 bcrypt regression via an unobserved code/flag change on auth-service
Shared neighbor degradation (redis-cache / kyc-provider) driving auth-service login faults
auth-service log.level INFO->WARN config change as trigger
